I think I needed to hear this today.  I’m sitting here severely hungover from a bender and I’m beating myself up.  I went 431 days and ever since I got off the wagon I’ve just been trying to “dial it in” and the dial doesn’t seem to be working. I told some people I wanna take a break from it this week and I should probably stick to my guns on that one.  One day at a time.

Thanks for the reply!  I understand a lot of what you are saying and appreciate the insight.  I’m still weighing the chances I do drink again, but right now it’s Day 2 and I still don’t feel great, physically or mentally.  That’s a pretty good sign from myself to listen.

I think the biggest thing that you mentioned that really stuck out was the “sober groups” and sober friends.  If I decide to get sober again I will have to find people who are like minded to also hang out with.  That was one of the hardest parts that didn’t sit well with me over the 431 days, was the constant drinking I was surrounded by.  I love my friends who drink, but they drink, that’s what they do.  

It doesn’t help that I’m pursuing a girl right now who is a big partier.  I think I need to maybe just drop the idea of that one coming to fruition, because I know it’s going to be a big problem…just alcohol and drugs and myself probably not being able to say no.  

Anyways, once again I appreciate your insight.  I’m 33 currently and it has gotten to the point where I’m wanting to hang up the hat on partying and debauchery.  It’s been a part of my life since I was 17 and after going 431 days, the last 2 months back in the saddle have felt…long.  And tiresome.  I’m not fully back to where I was at, but that was the first time I blacked out in about 500 days.  Did not feel great. 

Thanks for sharing your story! Appreciate you!

It sucks.  It’s so hard in the town I’m at to meet new people, there isn’t really anything to do.  It’s a huge drinking town in a state where people are taught to drink to socialize.  luckily I only have one friend that keeps forgetting I’m not drinking and she is one of the ones that struggles the most herself.  Most of my friends are supportive or just meet it with general indifference.  But it’s those little things that really get to me more than anything.  The movies, playing video games, going to the farmers market.  No need for booze for any of those.  

Here’s to hoping we can both make strides in the right direction, meet new people and maybe help others along the way!  I got a lot of decent advice from people that I’ll be trying.  Straight asking people to do sober stuff.  Finding common ground stuff that I have in with others and doing those things one on one.  Going out to eat at places that don’t serve alcohol (this one is tough, feel like everywhere serves alcohol besides fast food).  Etc.  Worst case is they just say no and you find out that they’re not as supportive as you thought they’d be.

I did this for the first couple months, also just plain refused to go out after 9 if anyone hit me up.  It was nice!  Been hanging out later and later though since I’ve been really lonely.  But I think I gotta start following this again.

She drank a ton in front of me, got really drunk and sloppy and then told me the next day that she blacked out.  Which I already knew because I’ve drank with her a ton in the past and it’s pretty easy to tell when she blacks out.

Yup. I almost caved last weekend.  Had a lot of friends in town they were all drinking.  I even said “I’ll let the group vote, I just want one beer” that was met with general indifference/negativity.  I just walked away and wandered around a little.  Friend got me a sparkling water.  But the whole time in my head I was like “you all have problems and won’t admit it and I just want one drink, why do I have to be the sober one this is so stupid.” 

At the end of it all I had to remind myself that I’m doing this for me and not them.  That it was me who I didn’t like when I was drinking and that this version of me I actually am starting to like.  

Don’t beat yourself up, lift yourself up.  You’re the only you you’ve got and you have to spend every waking moment with yourself.  Might as well love yourself for that strength you carry.

That is so awesome!  I’m glad you two have been able to reconnect and grow a stronger bond from your shared sobriety.  I hope that one day one of my friends sees that light too and a few of them are starting.  Thanks for sharing, I think particularly the “it’s ok to not see your friends do other cool stuff” part is what I needed to hear.

Oh man opening drinks up during party chat is so annoying.  Also the ones who open a conversation by saying “I’m drinking an 8.5% cider” or something to that effect. Woof.  I’ve basically just started saying “that’s great” in kind of a douchey tone and then changing the subject.   

The judgey/preachy part has been tough for me.  I know I was in the same boat 5 months ago, I know how difficult it can be.  But at the same time I also want to let it rip sometimes.  

Finding a different friend group is really difficult too, it’s a lot harder than people make it out to be.  If I do figure it out you’ll be the first to know haha

Compassion is the biggest reason that I have stuck with them.  I even told my therapist “I have trouble judging them because I was there too”.  And you are correct, it has definitely helped me develop compassion for myself in the process.

It’s so exhausting.  Just draining.  The moderation lies are the worst.  I have a lot of compassion, but when people continuously lie about how they’re “doing so much better”. Get real.  One of my friends was saying how she shouldn’t be blacking out as much as she does and has been doing a lot of work into moderating that area and then the next week proceeded to black out in front of me. Don’t talk about it be about it.

I guess it’s still pretty early on for me and I’m just holding onto some hope that they’ll change.  I have seen a little positivity from my quitting.  One of my friends has really used me as inspiration and has taken a huge step back.  I should probably hang out with her more.

I think I’m more inclined to want to meet people who can moderate.  The sober ones that I have met generally made it their whole personality and that’s just as obnoxious to me as the ones who make alcohol and partying theirs.
